claims.text: MOA: beta-lactam; binds and inactivates enzymes required for bacterial cell wall synth.
claims.quote: All beta-lactams bind to and inactivate enzymes required for bacterial cell wall synthesis.
Monobactams are parenteral beta-lactam bactericidal antibiotics.

claims.text: Treats: like ceftazidime vs Enterobacterales w.o AmpC/ESBL/KPC and P. aeruginosa; not anaerobes; gram (+) bacteria are resistant.
claims.quote: Aztreonam has activity similar to that of ceftazidime against Enterobacterales that do not produce AmpC beta-lactamase, extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL), or Klebsiella pneumoniae carbapenemase (KPC) Pseudomonas aeruginosa Aztreonam is not active against anaerobes. Gram-positive bacteria are resistant to aztreonam (in contrast to cephalosporins). Aztreonam acts synergistically with aminoglycosides.

claims.text: Allergy: cross-hypersensitivity unlikely (except ceftazidime, cefiderocol: similar R1 side chain), so it's used mainly for severe aerobic gram (-) infections in pts w a serious beta-lactam allergy.
claims.quote: Aztreonam shares structural similarities with few other beta-lactams, making cross-hypersensitivity unlikely, except with ceftazidime and cefiderocol, which have similar R1 side chains. Thus, aztreonam is used mainly for severe aerobic gram-negative bacillary infections (including meningitis) in patients who have a serious beta-lactam allergy but who nevertheless require beta-lactam therapy.

claims.text: Know: add other abx for suspected gram (+) or anaerobes; dose reduced in renal failure.
claims.quote: Other antibiotics are added to cover any suspected gram-positive species or anaerobes. The dose of aztreonam is reduced in renal failure.
